title: The DOCX editor read every offset three bytes low on a byte-order-marked main document, and called the result malformed
decision: retained, implemented in litchi-docx as a correctness fix
code_state: crates/litchi-docx/src/writer/doc/ only (doc.rs, doc/package.rs, doc/model.rs, doc/tests.rs); no public API signature, error type, limit or defence changed; no new unsafe and no new dependency; the crate remains #![forbid(unsafe_code)]
reason_codes: change 0638 reported that Package::document_mut() refuses alt-chunk-header.docx with 'invalid DOCX XML: syntax error: tag not closed' while Package::open admits it and Package::save republishes it, and could not chase it because no file under crates/ could change there

the mechanism is quick-xml 0.41.0 removing a leading UTF-8 byte order mark from the slice without counting it in Reader::buffer_position, so DocumentBody::from_xml's preserved ranges begin and end three bytes early and every body child is truncated inside its own closing tag

the reader is unaffected because DocumentPart::from_part parses the markup-compatibility-normalized output, which carries no mark; the probe asserts reader_bom part=true view=false on every marked input
same bytes, valid document, reader right and editor wrong, so the brief's fix branch applies rather than its freeze branch
the minimal constructed witness is five elements long: a marked document with one paragraph, refused before and accepted after, its unmarked twin accepted on both legs

accepted_evidence.corpus_census: a retained probe over ten documented aspects of all 63 DOCX-family fixtures under test-data/ on both legs: open, reader text and paragraph count, mark presence in the part and in the reader's view, sections, document_mut, no-op save, document_mut-then-save, the managed edit_document route, one-paragraph edit and save, and reopening the edited artifact
accepted_evidence.value_identity: diff of the two 630-line censuses yields three changed lines, all on alt-chunk-header.docx and all refusal text; all 55 no-op, 53 editor-touched, 54 managed-route and 50 edited published SHA-256 digests are identical between legs, as are the reader's paragraph counts and text lengths
accepted_evidence.bom_presence: a separate census of whether each fixture's word/document.xml starts with EF BB BF: exactly one of 63 does
accepted_evidence.witnesses: fourteen retained XML inputs run through MutableDocument::from_xml on both legs, including a four-step bisection of the fixture's own part and a five-element minimal reproduction
accepted_evidence.constructed_packages: four packages rebuilt from two tracked fixtures by a retained script, differing only in the mark, one pair with markup-compatibility markup in the main document and one without
accepted_evidence.unit_tests: three tests in crates/litchi-docx/src/writer/doc/tests.rs covering range identity, the mark's survival across an appended paragraph, and the frozen body-final section placement refusal with and without the mark

accepted_costs.no_timing: no timing was taken; the change adds one three-byte prefix comparison to a path that already parses the whole part and is not shared with the reader, so no paired measurement or A/A floor is reported
accepted_costs.refusal_moves: on a marked main document document_mut() stops refusing, so a caller that edits and saves now meets a later typed refusal from the OPC publication audit instead of an early false one; the save stays atomic and no partial package is published
accepted_costs.synthetic_reach: exactly one fixture in the repository is marked, so the newly admitted class is represented by constructed packages rather than by real producer output

known_gaps.sectpr_placement: alt-chunk-header.docx places w:altChunk after the body-final w:sectPr; the editor and the managed transaction refuse it, the reader admits it. ECMA-376 CT_Body makes the fixture schema-invalid, so the refusal is defensible, but the two routes disagree. Frozen with witnesses w3-sect-then-altchunk.xml and w4-altchunk-then-sect.xml; not resolved here
known_gaps.strict_universal_measure: strict.docx is an ISO Strict document whose w:pgSz is '612pt'; crates/litchi-docx/src/writer/section/codec/xml.rs:409 parses it with parse_u32, which admits only ST_UnsignedDecimalNumber, so document_mut() refuses while the reader opens the file and reads its section. A feature gap in the mutable section model, identical on both legs, frozen for its own record
known_gaps.publication_audit_bom: crates/xml-minifier/src/audit.rs:1319 slices input.get(start..end) with Reader::buffer_position offsets, so a regenerated marked part is refused at publication with 'malformed XML at byte 0: invalid XML declaration boundary'. The same crate's streaming auditor handles the mark explicitly; only the slice auditor does not. Out of this change's scope by the brief: reported, not touched
known_gaps.managed_transaction_bom: crate::document::Snapshot mixes quick-xml positions with its own buffer the same way, refusing a marked dense body with "expected '</w:bo<w:p>'" identically on both legs. Not fixed here: that route carries source-backed splice reservations and exact-source byte proofs and needs its own value-identity argument
known_gaps.end_to_end: because of the two gaps above, editing a marked DOCX and saving it still does not work end to end; this change removes the first of four obstacles and makes the diagnosis accurate

withheld: any timing, allocation, instruction-count, throughput or registered performance result
any claim that a byte-order-marked DOCX can be edited and republished end to end
